target_customer: Restaurants, hotels and food businesses in Nigeria and Ghana that buy food supplies
problem: Restaurants buy through expensive middlemen or send staff to open markets with inflated prices, wasting time and money.
business_model: B2B marketplace take rate and margin on supplies, plus ERP software and buy-now-pay-later
product_category: B2B food supply marketplace and procurement

founders.name: Tunde Kara
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built brands and ran projects for Samsung, Coca-Cola, Google and General Electric without saying he was employed there.

founders.name: Wale Oyepeju
founders.background_notes: YC page: 13 years of technology experience including projects for MTN Nigeria and Sony.

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace and ordering app are standard engineering; the difficulty is logistics, supplier sourcing and credit.

defensibility.rationale: Supplier relationships and logistics scale help, but thin margins and many B2B commerce rivals limit the moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Vendease restructured in 2024 and 2025 instead.

market_need_then: Restaurants faced middlemen markups and market trips; TechCrunch covered the company in March 2021 as an Amazon-style supplier for restaurants.

branding.domain_note: Used vendease.com, which now redirects to dscvrfrsh.com as of the fetch; relationship to a rename is unconfirmed.

identity.visual_style: Brand refresh evolved it from a utility tool into a tech-forward ecosystem (freelance portfolio)

brand_strength.rationale: Known in Nigerian startup press but no evidence of community, mascot or brand-led growth.

outcome_analysis: Vendease raised a $3.2M seed in October 2021 and a $30M Series A package in September 2022 ($20M equity, $10M debt), but then cut 9% of staff in November 2022, 68 people in September 2024 and about 120 in February 2025 while restructuring toward profitability, and its CFO left in 2025. The record points to growth that outran margins in a tough funding climate; no shutdown is reported.
notes: Series A reported as 30M total with 20M equity and 10M debt; one outlet headline says 20M. Layoff percentages in February 2025 conflict (44% vs 35%). Competitors TradeDepot, Kaso and Awesome Fresh appear only in undated aggregator lists, so the competitor list is empty. The seed investors were taken from the Series A coverage, which calls Hustle Fund and Hack VC previous investors. Founder education not found. The vendease.com redirect to dscvrfrsh.com was seen once and not explained by any source.
